title: The band that did not speak off stage; Duke the politician
summary: Willard and Jones remark that Ellington's men stayed distant yet played together, and Strayhorn says Duke never noticed a missing saxophonist.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: (Inaudible)
Oh, yeah. We got along very well. And well, I got along with the band well. It was -- they treated me good.
They were a beautiful bunch of people.
Yeah. They treated me very good.
I don't think they got along with each other.
No. Yeah, that's right.
They were difficult to be around.
That's well stated, because I guess they'd been getting on each other's nerves, after being out on the road so long.
What never fails to amaze me is that they wouldn't speak on the band bus sometimes. No two members of the band would speak to each other, but yet they'd get on the stand --
Oh, they could play, play together.
You know, they were all very close, but see them off the stand and they didn't seem at all close to each other.

No. No, not at all. I think it was -- I think it was the most unique outfit that I've ever seen, you know, as far as the personnel, as you were saying, you know, how they were very courteous to everybody that wasn't in the

band, but when they got on the stand to play, they were quite together, you know? And Ellington had to be a great politician to keep those guys, all of those drunks, in the band, and to keep them playing. There was one time when in Basin Street East, you know they have a high bandstand there, so I don't remember whether Paul fell off or he didn't come back from -- around 3rd Avenue where that little bar was, where they'd take intermission, you know?
Uh-huh.

So Duke was playing with four saxophones, and Strayhorn was still on his feet at that point, and I brought up the question. I said, "Doesn't Duke -- doesn't it bother Duke?" And Strayhorn says, "He doesn't know that he's not there."
(Laughter)
And the band sounded just as good, because of the way it was voiced, you know. There was no such thing as really a first man, you know? He said, "Duke doesn't even know he's missing."
(Laughter)
With that group maybe it was practical to write that way, right?
Yeah, you know?
Somebody is liable to be missing.
